(1) THE SHAPE AND WHY: an event marker (test_run), an optional test_recipients override, and an unconditional TEST_FORBIDDEN_RECIPIENTS filter that runs LAST, with an empty resolved envelope meaning NO SEND. Chosen over mutating the producer's EMAIL_RECIPIENT (a two-deploy dance around a live monthly schedule, with a window in which the 10-01 fire would deliver to the wrong set) and over 'no send at all on a test invocation' (which the face permitted but which would make EG-s-21's FWD-10 unprovable by construction: FWD-10's content is that the terminal send FIRES and reaches andrew@). A filter rather than a replacement because a replacement is a DEFAULT and a default is defeated by the next caller who passes an override. (2) WHAT A FUTURE READER MUST DO TO KEEP THE JOINT DELIVERY: never add the marker to aws_scheduler_schedule.monthly_run's input (it sends jsonencode({mode = 'run'}); a marker there would silently narrow the monthly report to andrew@ and nothing would alarm); never resolve recipients anywhere but _resolve_recipients (the EMAIL_RECIPIENTS global is still exported for EG-s-9's battery, so reaching for it directly is an available mistake that would re-open this gap); and keep test_the_scheduled_invocation_is_unchanged_and_still_reaches_both, which is the only mechanical thing standing between a future 'safety' tightening and a silently narrowed monthly report. (3) WOULD IT HAVE CAUGHT ROUND 1'S DEFECT: yes, and not as a retrospective claim -- test_producer_shaped_document_fires_exactly_one_terminal_send WAS RUN against the pre-fix blob this session and failed with 'exactly ONE terminal send on the refusal branch', zero sends. The round-1 arms could not have caught it because every one of them fed the consumer's own assumption back to the consumer; the producer was never in the loop. The transferable form is 'build the fixture from the producer, not the docstring', and the docstring that misled round 1 is corrected in place. (4) WHAT REMAINS UNTESTED: (i) the send has still never fired in production -- this order proves the guard is TRUTHY on the producer's real document and that _send_terminal_unresolved is called with those rows in a stubbed harness, not that SES accepted anything; (ii) EMISSION IS NOT DELIVERY -- the new MessageId line proves an id was returned, and whether the message reached andrew@'s inbox is an inbox read no arm here takes; (iii) the refusal branch is unexercised end to end (round 1's driven run produced PUBLISH because its holes classified D and the gate refuses only on class C), which is EG-s-21's entire subject; (iv) the provider column will read '(not stated)' on every row of a real terminal email because the producer writes that field only into coverage_egress_ask.json -- the email is honest about it now rather than printing 'None', but closing the gap is a producer change nobody owns.
